headline: RAB dissolved, replaced by new Special Response Battalion
summary: The elite force is replaced by the SRB, though assets and manpower are transferred to the new unit.
details: The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has been officially dissolved and replaced by the new Special Response Battalion (SRB), following a gazette notification on Tuesday.
Under the SRB Act, all of RAB's powers, facilities, funds, manpower, assets, and liabilities have been transferred to the new specialized police unit.

The SRB will be formed through postings or deputations of personnel from the police and other disciplined forces, with its director general being a police officer of at least additional inspector general rank.
RAB, formed in 2004, faced mounting criticism and US sanctions in 2021 over allegations of extrajudicial killings and human rights violations.
The move follows calls for dissolution from the UN, the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, and various international rights organizations.

While Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that SRB has no connection to the former force, opposition members in parliament argued that the change is merely a shell change as the structure and facilities remain.
caption:
RAB is gone. A new force, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), takes its place.

The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has been officially dissolved and replaced by the new Special Response Battalion (SRB), following a gazette notification on Tuesday.

Under the SRB Act, all of RAB's powers, facilities, funds, manpower, assets, and liabilities have been transferred to the new specialized police unit.

The SRB will be formed through postings or deputations of personnel from the police and other disciplined forces, with its director general being a police officer of at least additional inspector general rank.

RAB, formed in 2004, faced mounting criticism and US sanctions in 2021 over allegations of extrajudicial killings and human rights violations.

The move follows calls for dissolution from the UN, the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, and various international rights organizations.

While Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that SRB has no connection to the former force, opposition members in parliament argued that the change is merely a shell change as the structure and facilities remain.

headline_marked: Tk 2.5 lakh crore: [[Three metro rail projects approved]] for Dhaka
headline: Tk 2.5 lakh crore: Three metro rail projects approved for Dhaka
summary: The government has cleared the construction of MRT Line-5 Southern route and cost revisions for MRT Line-1 and Line-5 Northern route to expand the city's mass transit.
details: The government has approved the construction of three metro rail lines for Dhaka at an estimated cost of nearly Tk 2.5 lakh crore. The approval includes the new MRT Line-5 Southern route and cost revisions for MRT Line-1 and MRT Line-5 Northern route.

The MRT Line-5 Southern route, costing Tk 45,504 crore, will run from Gabtoli to Dasherkandi via Kalyanpur, Shyamoli, and Hatirjheel. It will feature 15 stations, with 11 underground and four overground, and is expected to be completed by August 2033.

Once operational, the journey from Gabtoli to Dasherkandi will be reduced to 28 minutes, with trains running every four minutes and 30 seconds. The route will be serviced by 19 trains, each with six air-conditioned coaches.

The MRT-5 Northern route from Hemayetpur to Bhatara now costs Tk 89,848 crore due to a 118 percent cost escalation. The project is now slated for completion in December 2032, with JICA's loan share increasing significantly.

The MRT Line-1 project, which has seen a cost escalation of 117 percent, will now cost Tk 114,394 crore and finish in December 2033. It will run from Kamalapur to Kuril, with branches to the airport and Purbachal.

Cost increases across the projects are attributed to the devaluation of the taka against the dollar, global inflation, higher construction material costs, and changes in project design. Contractors also added risk premiums for underground construction in densely populated areas.
State Minister for Planning Zonayed Saki noted that the projects were approved now to secure current loan interest rates from JICA before they potentially increase to 3.50 percent by September.
